..
Issued at 203 PM CDT Tue Sep 1 2026

A negative tilted shortwave (originating from the southwestern 
US/monsoonal moisture) will continue to track northeast over the 
region with additional shortwave energy developing on the southern 
tail of this wave over the eastern half of SD/NE into MN through 
late tonight. At the surface, a stationary boundary lies south of 
the CWA extending through central/northern NE into IA as a high 
pressure system lies just to the north of the CWA over ND. With this 
mid level moisture, current radar indicates scattered rain (and a 
few embedded weak thunderstorms) with HREF paintballs/NBM indicating 
a gradual northeast track across the CWA with additional development 
of showers and thunderstorms (forcing from this secondary energy 
aloft) this afternoon/evening through late tonight. Did a blend of 
HREF/NBM for pops through 12Z Wednesday. As the shortwave exits the 
region, the last of the convection is forecast to exit eastern SD/MN 
by 12Z Wednesday.

Instability wise, HREF mean MUCAPE runs from 500 to about 1000j/kg 
south of highway 12 with the highest values over far south central 
SD. Bulk shear ranges from 30-50kts over the CWA, highest over south 
central through east central SD with the overall better forcing and 
instability lying south/southeast of the CWA. Dewpoints will rise 
into the lower to mid 60s over this area with ample amounts of low 
and mid level moisture as PWATs run between 1.3 to 1.6" over the 
southern half of the CWA (gradient increasing further south you go) 
which runs between 92 to 97th percentile per climo for this time of 
year. Latest HREF mean 2-5km UH>75ms2s indicates the bulk of this 
potential organized convection developing over SD/NE border between 
~22-00Z along the SD/NE border and tracking northeastward through 
southeastern SD into MN with portions of south central to east 
central possibly being clipped being on the northern side of the 
convection. 2-5km UH>150m2s2 indicates supercell potential with most 
of the HREF models keeping this threat again south of the CWA. 
Looking at the HRRR/REFS specifically, it does indicate discrete 
cells developing over south central/southern SD (potentially 
supercells), as 0-3km SRH is up to around 400m2s2 around 00Z, with 
additional development/storm mergers with storms potentially growing 
upscale into a condensed bowing segment over southeastern SD into 
MN. Otherwise north of this, isolated cells or clusters (potentially 
strong to severe) will track across central through northeastern 
SD/MN late tonight early AM mainly east of the Mo River. There is a 
bit of a difference in CAMs on exact storm mode and track at this 
time so low confidence exists on exact outcome.

With this threat, the SPC has shifted the Slight Risk (level 2/5) a 
bit more southward due to the latest HREF run with the slight risk 
along and east of a line from Murdo to Miller with a Marginal Risk 
(level 1/5) north and northwest of the slight risk mainly from 
Pierre to Gettysburg and eastward. The main threats will be large 
hail, quarter to golfball sized, with the potential for 2"+ in 
diameter within the cig 1 hatched area over southeast Jones, Lyman, 
Buffalo, and the southern half of Hyde/Hand counties per the 
supercell threat. With this threat of supercells, this hatched area 
is also highlighted in a 2% tornado risk being closer to the frontal 
boundary as hodographs are curved over far south central, southern, 
and southeastern SD this afternoon and evening. STP is under 1 with 
0-1km shear running between 15-20kts and 0-1km SRH between 100-
200m2s3. Wind gusts of 60-75 mph with a hatched area over southern 
Lyman County and eastward through southeastern SD. Due to higher 
PWATs, any slow moving and stronger storms could lead to heavy 
rainfall. 

With high pressure and winds mainly out of the east and recent rains 
leads to the possibility of upslope fog along the eastern slopes of 
the Coteau early Wednesday morning. Otherwise, continuing in 
southwest flow aloft, another shortwave will move in over the region 
Wednesday night/Thursday morning. With lack of instability and weak 
forcing, there is really only spotty chances of moisture over 
portions of south central SD for now per NBM. Additional threat of 
showers and thunderstorms are possible over far northeastern SD/MN 
Thursday afternoon and evening, associated with a surface low, with 
the higher pops and instability to our northeast closer to the low. 
Otherwise a trough deepens over the western CONUS by the end of the 
week and weekend which will amplify the ridge overhead with really 
only sight chance of pops here and there for the weekend. Highs will 
overall warm into the upper 80s to the lower 90s Thursday-Saturday, 
with Friday and Saturday temps around 10-20 degrees above average! 
Temps will gradually cool Sunday into early next week as the ridge 
breaks down and cold front moves through.
